acceptance_criteria.notes: All requested commands are green, with no provider calls (OPENROUTER_API_KEY unset). crew-core: 77/77 on the interpreter and on --bytecode --strict-bytecode, including the two compaction tests. claims-test, sample-test and scenario-pack-test pass (EXIT 0). crew-sim --turns 60 --seeds 1..5 gives tick 60 and errors 0 for both consent and orders, with 150-210 answers per session, so compaction is exercised in real runs. Re-running --check for news-decades-late and light-from-the-dead over seeds 1..20 is byte-identical to review/*.claims.txt. Deductions: the design asks for an id-uniqueness compaction test and none exists; the harness checks 60 turns over seeds 1..3, not 1..5 (I verified 1..5 by hand); I did not run validate (as instructed).

correctness_robustness.notes: Compaction is sound. 'Expired' (expires <= tick) matches the stale check (tick >= expires), so an answer that can still be retried is never dropped (tested). Nothing outside complete/ask reads the bank, so conversation issues that keep a dropped request id are harmless. Median and quantile interpolation, mean and share all match their definitions. crew-sample's budget accounting is right: f.calls is counted even when a fetch fails, each fetch makes at most 1 call, and the remaining budget is passed down. Deductions: refusal_reasons.<anything> is accepted, so a typo passes as 0 (verified); three pack claims credit an individual but measure a ship-wide counter; once compacted, a dropped id can be reused; the watch guide text still hardcodes the default ship; crew-sample silently drops seeds whose play fails.

test_quality.notes: Good: the determinism cmp, a deliberately changed ship that makes a named claim fail with exit 1, six malformed-claim cases, and a stub run that checks the budget. Gaps: no id-reuse or uniqueness test; no test for claim (4), neither the watch with a non-default crew nor narrativeText rejecting work_/rest_; no malformed cases for a share value outside 0..1, 'when' on a non-share claim, or a refusal_reasons typo; claims.ail is tested only on the interpreter (other targets run both engines), and 4 of its 9 properties are skipped for lack of a generator.

docs_bookkeeping.notes: The crew_core and crew-lab CHANGELOGs, AGENT.md and README are accurate and specific. REVIEW.md: 33/36, the three FAIL lines, 60 moments with words, 0 narrative failures and the quoted lines all match review/. Deductions: there is no .ailang/state/sprints/sprint_S-CREW-VERIFY-LOOP.json; every M1-M4 checkbox in crew-verify-loop-sprint.md is still unchecked; REVIEW's '62 provider calls in total' cannot be reconciled with review/*.samples.ndjson (which sum to 14 calls; the rest presumably came from an unrecorded first round, as did the '98 first-round lines'); the README points at ~/.ailang/crew-lab-stapledon, a home outside the repo; the working tree has uncommitted lockfile generated_at churn.

defects.issue: metricOK accepts refusal_reasons.<any 1..64 chars>, so a mistyped reason code reads as 0 and passes. '{metric: refusal_reasons.no_such_reasn, stat: max, op: ==, value: 0}' printed PASS with exit 0. This contradicts the design and README promise that a typo can't pass as 0.
defects.suggestion: Validate against the finite set of social_dynamics refusal codes (insufficient_resource, ...).

defects.issue: medic-asks-for-relief (relief.asked), skeptic-pushes-back (replies.decline) and engineer-gets-relief-with-consent (relief.granted) are worded and noted as one crew member's behaviour but measure ship-wide counters, so they can PASS because of someone else. The claim language has no per-crew relief or reply measure.
defects.suggestion: Add crew.<id>.replies.<label> and relief measures, or rename and re-note these claims as ship-wide.

defects.issue: After compaction, ask() accepts an id that a dropped bank entry used, since it checks only pending and the retained bank. Domain ids derived from it (answer-/concern-/relief-${id}) and conversation issues could then collide with history. This is documented as a host contract ('the watch and crew-sim never reuse ids'), but nothing enforces it and nothing tests it. The design's acceptance item 'ids unique among retained/pending' has no test.
defects.suggestion: Add a test that pins the behaviour (a reuse is rejected or is safe), or keep a compact set of seen ids.

defects.issue: Claim (4) says the watch works for any scenario's crew, but the Guide/help text still says 'Five specialists prepare for possible first contact' and 'Archive compute is reusable capacity for Spire analysis. Replacement modules and diagnostic cartridges...'. A Stapledon scenario shows the wrong ship in its help. No test covers a non-default crew in the watch.
defects.suggestion: Derive the help text from the scenario, or make it generic; add a presenter test with a 3-crew scenario.

defects.issue: The legacy watch guide still says the response policy limit is 'maximum8'; the limit is now 64.
playKeeping errors are swallowed with Err(_) => [], so a seed that fails to play disappears from the sample with no message.
defects.suggestion: Report the error and exit 1, as crew-sim does.

defects.issue: A non-string 'note' (e.g. 7) or 'captain' is silently read as "". For note, the claim is accepted with the note dropped.
claims-test runs claims.ail tests only on the interpreter, not with --bytecode --strict-bytecode as reply-test does; 4 of 9 properties are skipped (no generator for [Json]).

'62 provider calls in total' and '5 of 98 first-round lines' cannot be checked against review/: the committed samples record 14 calls in total (2+2+1+3+3+3) and 60 moments, all from cache or generated.
defects.suggestion: State that the counts include an earlier round, or commit that round's log.

defects.issue: The README says ~/.ailang/crew-lab-stapledon 'holds the words already sampled', but that home is on the executor's machine and isn't in the repo, so other reviewers trigger new calls.
defects.suggestion: Say that it's local, or ship the cache.

defects.issue: There is no sprint JSON, and every M1-M4 checkbox is unchecked although the work landed.
defects.suggestion: Create and update the sprint JSON and tick the plan.

summary: PASS, 77/100. Compaction is correct: only answers whose requests have expired (expires <= tick, consistent with the stale check) are dropped, and only when the bank is full. Live retries survive, and 60-turn runs are clean with 150+ answers per session. crew-sim --check, crew-sample and the Stapledon pack all work, deterministically and without a provider, and REVIEW's claim results reproduce byte-for-byte. Main issues: refusal_reasons typos pass as 0 (verified); three pack claims credit individuals but use ship-wide metrics; dropped ids can be reused (untested); the watch help still hardcodes the default ship; no sprint JSON and the plan checkboxes are unchecked; REVIEW's call counts can't be reconciled with the committed samples.
